reply_text:
I wouldn't merge this yet. `extensionOf` doesn't follow the rule the README sets out, and since the content type is looked up from the extension, uppercase or multi-dot filenames get the wrong one. I ran the tests and some edge cases on my side and didn't change anything in the repo.

**Blocker: `src/extension.js`**
```js
return name.split('.')[1];
```
The README says the extension is the text after the **last** dot, lowercased. This code takes the text after the **first** dot and keeps its case. What I saw:

| filename | got | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `Archive.TAR.GZ` | `"TAR"` → octet-stream | `gz` → application/gzip |
| `photo.JPG` | `"JPG"` → octet-stream | `jpg` → image/jpeg |
| `my.photo.jpg` | `"photo"` → octet-stream | `jpg` → image/jpeg |
| `README` | `undefined` | `""` |

So uppercase or multi-dot names, which are common from cameras and archives, all fall back to `application/octet-stream`. Returning `undefined` instead of `""` also breaks the README's rule for names with no dot. A fix would look something like:
```js
const i = name.lastIndexOf('.');
return i === -1 ? '' : name.slice(i + 1).toLowerCase();
```

**Tests are too thin.** The only extension test is `photo.jpg`, which passes with either version of the code, so it didn't catch the bug. It needs cases for the README's own examples (`Archive.TAR.GZ`, `photo.JPG`), a name with no dot, a trailing dot, and a few `contentType` checks.

**`safeName` looks fine.** Slashes and backslashes are replaced, so `a/../../etc/passwd` becomes `a_.._.._etc_passwd`, which can't move up a directory. One thing to handle: names like `...` or `.` turn into an empty string. The caller should reject that or use a fallback name, because an empty stored name could mean writing to the upload directory itself.

**Minor:**
- The changelog for 0.5.0 doesn't mention the new filename sanitizing (`safeName`).
- Under the last-dot rule `.bashrc` has extension `bashrc`. That matches the README as written. I'm only flagging it in case dotfiles should count as having no extension.

The version bump and the README additions look fine.
